title: Heuristic-guided recommendations flow and edge-case notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an early wireframe + interaction writeup for a heuristic-guided recommendations panel in Optimize. Focus: batching, caching and quantization suggestions for inference workloads. Goal is to prototype a guided surface that a workload owner (ML eng / infra engineer / SRE) can use to quickly evaluate economically sensible changes, preview trade-offs, and safely apply or export presets.

Scope & audience:
- Primary: product-optimize PMs and UX, engine/serving PMs, solutions engineers testing suggestions with customers.
- Secondary: SREs and platform teams who will operationalize rollouts.

High-level flows (three modes):
1) Quick-Apply (one-click presets)
   - User selects workload from left nav -> the UI surfaces 1–3 recommended preset cards (e.g., "Safe Cost Save", "Aggressive Quant", "Latency-first").
   - Each preset shows: expected cost delta, 95th P90 latency delta, confidence score, small list of changed knobs (batch size, cache TTL, quant profile).
   - CTA: Dry-run / Apply to staging / Apply to production (Apply requires approval if > X% cost change).

2) Guided Walkthrough (explainable stepper)
   - Step 1: Observed workload profile summary (QPS, avg seq len, peak distribution).
   - Step 2: Why we recommend each action (heuristic reasons: low prefix reuse -> low benefit from caching; high seq-length variance -> batching limited).
   - Step 3: Simulation preview with token-level cost projection and a small synthetic roll-forward showing 7-day estimated spend and latency distribution.

3) Expert mode (manual tuning + sandbox)
   - Full list of actionable knobs with inline explainers and a simulation slider.
   - Recommender suggests a baseline, but user can tweak and re-simulate.

Core UI components (wireframe text):
- Left: Workload selector (search + tags: route, model, region, customer).
- Middle: Recommendation pane (stacked cards). Card fields: title, top-3 knobs changed, impact badges (cost%, latency ms), confidence pill (color-coded), quick-preview sparkline (cost over 7d).
- Right: Impact inspector (metric deltas, risk notes, diffs), one-click Open in Console button, Release controls (canary %, target fleet).
- Top toolbar: Simulation toggle (on/off), timeframe selector, "compare to baseline" toggle.

ASCII wireframe excerpt:
[Workloads] | [Recommendation cards] | [Inspector]
- Search   | Card A               | Cost: -18%
- tags     | - Batch x2           | Latency P95: +2ms
          | - Cache TTL 120s      | Confidence: 0.74 (medium)
          | - Quant: int8         | Risks: potential quality regression for long-context prompts

Heuristics & scoring notes (how we rank suggestions):
- Score = weighted(sum of {cost_savings_estimate * econ_weight, latency_impact_penalty, quality_risk_penalty, rollout_complexity_penalty}).
- Confidence computed from signal depth: number of matching historical workloads + model family match + quant compatibility check.
- Economy-first presets bias weight to cost_savings_estimate; latency-first presets raise latency penalty weight.

Edge cases to document (must handle):
- Cold-start-heavy workloads: prefix caching suggestions may be noisy; show warning and low confidence.
- Multi-model routes: if a route sends to multiple architectures, flag potentially incompatible quantization suggestions.
- Privacy/air-gapped customer: forbid sending telemetry to hosted simulation; enable offline-sim mode (requires smaller sample).
- Low QPS routes: batching will not trigger often — recommend manual target-based batching instead of dynamic batching.
- Long-context specialization: quantization can degrade long-range attention — add a special QA check that runs a small set of user prompts through quantized variant in sandbox.

Simulation behavior & data needs:
- Input: 14-day trace sample (binned QPS, seq length distribution, token-level costs).
- Simulation output: cost delta, P50/P95 latency delta, expected tail error rate, estimated TPU/GPU utilization change.
- For offline (private) installs: support upload of CSV trace and run the sim locally (UI should render results without sending traces back).

Apply / rollout safety model:
- Default action: produce a canary rollout plan with automatic rollback threshold.
- Suggested plan includes: canary % (default 5%), monitoring windows (30m), indicators to watch (latency P95, error rate, quality regression metric if available).
- Require approval if predicted cost delta > 20% or if confidence < 0.6.

Example microcopy (short):
- Card confidence pill: "Confidence: Medium — based on 9 similar workloads"
- Impact caption: "Estimated cost change uses your last 14 days of traffic; results may vary during seasonal peaks."
- Apply CTA tooltip: "Dry-run runs a simulation and creates a config bundle for staging. Apply will create a rollout plan for this route."

Backlog & next steps (prioritized):
1) MVP data plumbing: hook sample trace endpoint + sim engine -> UI preview (must-have). Acceptance: accurate cost/latency numbers within 15% of offline sim. (Owner: Diego)
2) Preset UX: design 3 starter presets and test with 3 internal customers. Acceptance: user can apply preset in < 3 clicks and view rollout plan. (Owner: Rina)
3) Confidence score logic: implement simple heuristics; expose raw signals in inspector. Acceptance: show at least 3 signal sources in inspector. (Owner: Noah)
4) Offline sim for Private installs: PoC CLI that accepts CSV and returns sim JSON. (Owner: infra eng small team)
5) Safety & approvals: integrate with RBAC + approval flow; block direct apply for >20% cost changes. (Owner: product security)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Thresholds: what confidence cutoff should require manual approval? Proposal: 0.6.
- Preset naming & taxonomy: should we use economy/latency/quality axis, or more descriptive names derived from actual heuristics?
- Telemetry policy for hosted customers: how much raw input trace can we store for better sims? Needs legal signoff.
- Default canary size: 5% vs 10% for low-QPS routes — should be workload dependent.

Testing plan (early):
- Internal dogfood: pick 5 routes across hosted/dedicated/private and run A/B for two weeks. Collect cost and latency deltas and manual QA checks.
- Customer trial: invite three beta customers; require Solutions Eng escort for first two applying changes.

Notes for designers: 
- Keep cards scannable: emphasis on two numbers: cost % and P95 delta. Confidence is secondary but visible.
- Use neutral colors for medium confidence; red only for high risk.
- Provide animation for simulation progress and small sparkline to show baseline vs projected.

Unresolved UX frictions we spotted in hallway tests:
- Users want to compare suggestions side-by-side (multi-select cards). Add a temporary "compare" view.
- Some users prefer suggested knob-level rationales (e.g., "increase batch size because average seq length < 64"). Make it tappable and short.

Appendix: short example scenario
- Input: Route /chat/v1, model=llama-70b, avg seq len 120, QPS=8, burst to 40, baseline P95=210ms, current batching disabled, cache TTL 0s.
- Suggested preset: "Safe Cost Save" -> Batch x2, Cache TTL 60s, Quant: bf16->int8 (compatibility warning). Sim shows cost -14%, P95 +6ms, confidence 0.68.
- Action recommended: dry-run -> sandbox quant test with 10 canonical prompts -> if quality deltas <= 0.5 BLEU (example metric) then canary 5% for 1h.

-- end of notes --
